prompt.align: Which one is really longer? Line them up first.
prompt.order: Put them in order, shortest first.
prompt.indirect: Which is {ask}, {a} or {b}? They cannot move. Use the string.
prompt.attribute: Which is {ask}, {a} or {b}? What would you use to find out?

label.startLineHeld: Start line. Tap to move the {name} here.
label.onBench: {name} on the bench. Tap to pick it up.
label.inPool: {name}. Tap to put it in the next space.

status.tapToMove: Tap one that starts late, then tap the start line.
status.lined: They both start at the line now.
status.stringStart: First hold the string up to {a}.
status.stringCut: The string is as tall as {a}. Now take it to {b}.
status.stringCarried: The string is next to {b}. Compare them.

refuse.alignFirst: Line them up at the start line first.
refuse.fillFirst: Put all three in the spaces first.

wrong.align: They start together now. Look at the ends.
wrong.order: Not yet. Find the shortest one first.
wrong.indirect: Look at where the string reaches.
wrong.attribute: Which tool finds out how long, how heavy, or how much it holds?

pick.look: They start at the same line. Look at the other ends.
pick.longer: The one that ends further from the start line is longer.
pick.shorter: The one that ends nearer the start line is shorter.

pickVertical.look: They stand on the same floor. Look at the tops.
pickVertical.taller: The one whose top is higher is taller.
pickVertical.lower: The one whose top is lower is shorter.

align.look: One starts late. Tap it, then tap the start line.
align.worked: When both start at the line, the one that ends further away is longer.

order.look: The glowing one is the shortest. Put it first.
order.worked: Shortest first, then the middle one, then the longest.

indirect.look: Hold the string up to {a}, then take it to {b}.
indirect.taller: If the string reaches higher than {b}, then {a} is taller.
indirect.lower: If the string does not reach the top of {b}, then {a} is shorter.

attribute.look: Is the question how long, how heavy, or how much it holds?
attribute.worked: A ruler finds how long. A balance scale finds how heavy. A measuring jug finds how much it holds.

demo.compareIntro: Which is longer? They must start at the same place.
demo.compareTapLate: This one starts late. Tap it.
demo.compareAnswer: This one ends further away. It is longer!
demo.orderIntro: Put them in order, shortest first.
demo.orderShortest: This one is the shortest. Tap it.

prompt.compare: Which is {ask}, the {left} or the {right}? Put them on the balance.
prompt.cubes: How many cubes weigh the same as the {thing}? Make it balance.

status.weighFirst: Put them on the balance first.
status.tooFew: The {thing} side is down. Add cubes.
status.tooMany: The cube side is down. Take a cube off.

right.cubes: Yes! The {thing} weighs the same as {count} cubes.

wrong.compare: Look at which side went down.
wrong.cubes: The beam is not level yet.

compare.look: The heavier side goes down. The lighter side goes up.
compare.worked: Big things are not always heavy. Trust the balance, not the size.

cubes.look: Add cubes until the beam is level.
cubes.worked: When the beam is level, both sides weigh the same. Count the cubes.

prompt.pour: Which holds more, the {a} or the {b}? Pour each into cups.
prompt.cups: How many cups does the {thing} fill? Pour it out.
prompt.jug: How much water is in the jug?
prompt.fill: Fill the jug to the line: {target} {unit}.
prompt.which: Which holds more, a {a} or a {b}?

wrong.pour: Count the cups each one filled.
wrong.jug: Look at the top of the water, then the marks.
wrong.fill: Look at the top of the water and the line.
wrong.customary: Think how many small ones fill the big one.

pour.look: Pour each one into cups, then count the cups.
pour.worked: The one that fills more cups holds more, even if it looks smaller.

cups.look: Count each full cup, one by one.
cups.worked: Touch each cup as you count. The last number is how many.

jug.look: Look at the top of the water. Which mark is it on?
jug.worked: The marks go up by {step}. Count up from the last number below the water.

fill.look: Pour in water until the top reaches the dashed line.
fill.worked: The marks go up by {step}. Pour out a little if the water goes past the line.

customary.look: 2 cups fill a pint. 2 pints fill a quart. 4 quarts fill a gallon.
customary.worked: A gallon is 4 quarts, 8 pints, or 16 cups.

demo2.balanceIntro: Which is heavier? Use the balance.
demo2.balanceTap: Tap to put them on the balance.
demo2.balanceDown: This side went down. It is heavier!
demo2.pourIntro: Which holds more? Pour each into cups.
demo2.pourSecond: Now pour the bowl into cups.
demo2.pourAnswer: The bowl filled more cups. It holds more!
demo2.jugIntro: Find the top of the water.

prompt.lay: How many blocks long is the {thing}? Lay blocks along it.
prompt.spot: Two children measured the {thing}. Which row is right?
prompt.unit_more: Which needs more to measure the {thing}, cubes or rods?
prompt.unit_fewer: Which needs fewer to measure the {thing}, cubes or rods?
prompt.count: Now, how many blocks long is it?

status.coverFirst: Lay blocks until the {thing} is covered.
status.covered: The {thing} is covered. Count the blocks.
status.past: The blocks go past the end. Take one off.
status.rowRight: Yes, that row is right. Now count it.

right.unit: Yes! Small cubes need more; long rods need fewer.

wrong.lay: Count the blocks one by one.
wrong.spot: Look for a gap or an overlap.
wrong.count: Count the blocks in the right row.
wrong.unit: A small unit fits more times than a big one.

lay.look: Start at the end of the {thing}. Put each block right after the last one.
lay.worked: No gaps, no overlaps. Count the blocks.

spot.look: Look for a space between blocks, or blocks on top of each other.
spot.worked: Blocks must touch end to end, with no gaps and no overlaps.

unit.look: A rod is as long as {rod} cubes.
unit.worked: The smaller the unit, the more of them you need.

demo3.unitsIntro: How many blocks long is the pencil?
demo3.unitsMore: Lay one after another. No gaps.
demo3.unitsCount: It is covered. Count: 1, 2, 3, 4. Four blocks!

prompt.place: Measure the {thing}. Move it to the ruler first.
prompt.offset: This ruler is broken. How long is the {thing}?
prompt.difference: How much longer is the {a} than the {b}?
prompt.numberline_add: A ribbon is {start} cm long. You add {change} cm more. How long is it now?
prompt.numberline_cut: A ribbon is {start} cm long. You cut {change} cm off. How long is it now?
prompt.read_inch: How long is the {thing}, in inches?
prompt.read_inch_fraction: How long is the {thing}, in inches?
prompt.read_mm: How long is the {thing}, in mm?

status.pickUp: Now tap the 0 on the ruler.
status.edge: That is the edge of the ruler. Start at 0.
status.placed: The {thing} starts at 0. Where does it end?
status.drawFirst: Tap a mark on the ruler to draw the line.
status.tapLine: Tap the number line where it lands.

wrong.offset: Count the spaces, not the end number.
wrong.difference: Find both lengths, then take the short one from the long one.
wrong.inch: Count the small marks after the last whole inch.
wrong.mm: Count the small marks after the last cm.

read.look: The {thing} starts at 0. Look at the number where it ends.
read.worked: Starting at 0, the number at the end is the length.

offset.worked: Count the spaces from {start} to the end. Or take {start} from the end number.

draw.look: The line starts at 0. Find the {n}.

difference.worked: Take the short length from the long length.

inch.look: Each inch is split into 4 small parts. Two parts make a half.
inch.worked: Find the last whole inch, then count the small parts after it.

mm.look: Each cm has 10 small marks. Each is 1 mm.
mm.worked: Every cm is 10 mm. Count by 10s to the last cm, then count the small marks.

prompt.unit: Which unit would you use to measure {what}?

what.scissors: how long a pair of scissors is
what.walk: how far you walk to school
what.town: how far it is to the next town
what.train: how far a long train ride goes
what.can: how much a can of drink holds

ask.key: About how long is a key?
ask.pencil: About how long is a pencil?
ask.phone: About how long is a phone?
ask.book: About how long is a book?
ask.scissors: About how long are school scissors?
ask.door: About how tall is a door?
ask.bed: About how long is a bed?
ask.car: About how long is a car?
ask.bus: About how long is a bus?
ask.tree: About how tall is a big tree?
ask.walk: About how far is a walk to school?
ask.town: About how far is it to the next town?
ask.train: About how far does a long train ride go?

wrong.unit: Think how big it is: cm for small things, m for big things, km for long trips.
wrong.amount: Picture it next to you. Is it really that big?
wrong.unit_mass: Light things are weighed in g, heavy things in kg.
wrong.unit_capacity: A little drink is measured in ml, a lot of water in l.

bench.cm: 1 cm: as wide as a finger

unit.look: Think: is it smaller than you, bigger than you, or a long trip?
unit.worked: Small things: cm. Big things: m. Long trips: km.

amount.look: One answer is ten times too big or too small.
amount.worked: Compare it with something you know: a door is about 2 m tall.

unit_mass.look: Could you hold it on one finger, or do you need both arms?
unit_mass.worked: Light things: g. Heavy things: kg.

unit_capacity.look: Is it a sip or a lot of water?
unit_capacity.worked: A little: ml. A lot: l.

demo4.readEnd: Look at the end. It ends at 7.
demo4.placeTap: Tap the crayon to pick it up.
demo4.placeRead: Now it starts at 0. It ends at 5. It is 5 cm long.
demo4.drawDone: The line goes from 0 to 6. It is 6 cm long.
demo4.estimateIntro: About how tall is a door?
demo4.estimateThink: A door is taller than a grown-up, but not by much.
demo4.estimateTap: So a door is about 2 m, not 20 m.

prompt.g: How much does it weigh? Read the scale.
prompt.kg: How heavy is it? Read the scale.
prompt.oz: How much does it weigh, in pounds and ounces?

wrong.read: Look at the number the needle points to.
wrong.interval: Work out how much one small mark is worth.
wrong.kg: Find the number before the needle, then count the marks.
wrong.lb: 16 oz make 1 lb. Count the ounces after the last pound.

read.look: Follow the needle to the number it points at.
read.worked: The needle points right at a number: that is the weight.

interval.look: Find the number just before the needle.
interval.worked: From {from} to {to} there are {marks} steps, so each small mark is {step}.

kg.look: Find the number just before the needle.
kg.worked: Each small mark is {step} kg. Count on from the number.

lb.look: Each pound has 16 small marks: one for each ounce.
lb.worked: Find the last pound, then count the ounces after it.

prompt.negative: What temperature does it show? It may be below zero.
prompt.read_f: What temperature does it show, in °F?
prompt.warmer: It was {start} °C. It got {by} degrees warmer. What is it now?
prompt.colder: It was {start} °C. It got {by} degrees colder. What is it now?

wrong.read: Find the top of the red line and the number below it.
wrong.negative: Below zero, the numbers go down as you go down.
wrong.change: Warmer goes up, colder goes down. Count past zero.

read.look: Look at the top of the red line.
read.worked: Find the number below it, then count up the marks. Each mark is {step} degrees.

negative.worked: Find the number nearest the top of the line, then count the marks. Each mark is {step}.

change.look: Start at {start}. Colder goes down, warmer goes up.

t.juice: You pour {a} {u} of juice into a jug, then {b} {u} more. How much juice is in the jug?
t.jug: A jug holds {a} {u} of water. You pour out {b} {u}. How much water is left?
t.bottles: A big bottle holds {a} {u}. A small bottle holds {b} {u}. How much more does the big bottle hold?
t.flour: A bag has {a} {u} of flour. A cook uses {b} {u}. How much flour is left?
t.fruit: A basket of fruit weighs {a} {u}. You add vegetables that weigh {b} {u}. How much does the basket weigh now?
t.parcels: A red parcel weighs {a} {u}. A blue parcel weighs {b} {u}. How much heavier is the red parcel?
t.ribbon: A ribbon is {a} {u} long. You cut off {b} {u}. How long is it now?
t.tower: A tower of blocks is {a} {u} tall. You add {b} {u} more. How tall is it now?
t.plants: A sunflower is {a} {u} tall. A bean plant is {b} {u} tall. How much taller is the sunflower?

wrong.join: Put the two parts together: add.
wrong.compare: Find the difference: take the small one from the big one.

join.look: Both amounts go into one: is the answer bigger or smaller?
join.worked: The bar has two parts, {a} and {b}. Add them.

left.look: You start with {a} and some goes. Is the answer bigger or smaller?
left.worked: The whole bar is {a}. One part is {b}. The other part is {a} − {b}.

compare.look: Line the two amounts up. How much sticks out?

demo5.scaleIntro: How much does the flour weigh?
demo5.scaleBefore: Find the number before the needle: 600.
demo5.scaleSteps: Each small mark is 50 g. 600, then 650.
demo5.thermoTop: Find the top of the red line.
demo5.thermoCount: The number below it is 20. Count by 2s: 22, 24, 26.
demo5.storyIntro: A bag has 600 g of flour. A cook uses 250 g.
demo5.storyBar: The whole bar is 600 g. One part is 250 g.

sheet.draw: Use a ruler. Draw a line {n} {unit} long.

ruler.1: Read the number at the other end. Between numbers, count the small marks.

offset.0: Read the number at each end.
offset.1: Take the smaller number away from the bigger one.

difference.1: Take the shorter length away from the longer one.

numberline.1: Add on, or take away, the change.

draw.0: Put the ruler's 0 on a dot.
draw.1: Draw along the edge to the number.

scale.0: Find the number just before the needle.
scale.1: Work out what each small mark is worth, then count on.

thermo.0: Find the top of the line, and the number just below it.
thermo.1: Count up the marks. Below 0, count down past zero: −1, −2, −3.

change.1: Warmer: count up. Colder: count down, past 0 if you need to.

jug.0: Find the number just below the water.
jug.1: Work out what each small mark is worth, then count up.

fill.0: Find the number on the jug.

customary.0: 2 cups fill a pint, 2 pints a quart, 4 quarts a gallon.

story.0: Both amounts go into one: add.
story.1: Taken away, or how much more: subtract.

estimate.0: Think of something you know the size of, like your hand or a door.
estimate.1: Pick the unit or the amount that makes sense.
